calls.description: Judge calls (an upper bound: the adaptive phase can stop early).
calls.title: Calls

input_token_count.description: ``"exact"`` when the text was counted with the judge's tokenizer, ``"approximate"`` when it was estimated from characters (the judge names no tokenizer).
input_token_count.title: Input Token Count

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens (exact or approximate: ``input_token_count``) at one attempt per window; retries can take it towards ``requests_max`` times this count.
input_tokens.title: Input Tokens

output_tokens.description: Completion tokens (approximate), at one attempt per window.
output_tokens.title: Output Tokens

requests_max.description: Judge requests when every window retries to MAX_ATTEMPTS attempts (an unparseable answer and a refused request are both retried, and each attempt re-sends the prompt).
requests_max.title: Requests Max

requests_min.description: Judge requests at one attempt per window (the same count as ``calls``).
requests_min.title: Requests Min

wall_s.description: Wall time in seconds at the judge's concurrency (approximate).
wall_s.title: Wall S

JobState.description: One job a runner was handed for the run.

status.description: pending, running, completed, failed, cancelled or unknown (a runner that cannot say).

JobState.title: JobState

MirrorState.description:
What a mirror last did (``run status`` shows it).

``remote`` is the display form of the mirror URI (safe_url): userinfo, query
and fragment never reach the state file, ``run status --json`` or a log line. ``last_error`` is redacted the
same way: a state file written before this rule holds the full URI in a flush error's text.

lag_s.description: Seconds since the last successful upload.
lag_s.title: Lag S

MirrorState.title: MirrorState

RunState.description: Where a run stands: its status, every step, its judge requests, and its jobs when a runner holds it.

done.description: Whether the run is done: its status is terminal and no job of it is still running (or, between a job's phases, unresolved by its runner).
done.title: Done

metrics.description: `<system>/<metric>@<k>` -> value of every system but the judge's own order (the full report with confidence intervals: metrics/report.json).
metrics.title: Metrics

mirror.description: The mirror's last upload and lag, if mirrored.

note.description: Why the state is not the local manifest's own: read from a newer mirror, or derived from jobs that ended without recording it; and a submission that failed.
note.title: Note

runner.description: The job runner holding the run, if any.
runner.title: Runner

status.description: submitted, running, completed, partial, failed or cancelled.

steps.description: Every planned step in run order; one not started yet is pending.
steps.title: Steps

RunState.title: RunState

StageEstimate.description: One stage's share of a CostEstimate.
StageEstimate.title: StageEstimate

StepProgress.description: How far a judging step has got, in judge windows.

done.description: Windows judged and stored so far.
done.title: Done

planned.description: The windows the step's schedule asks at most for its pools (the tournament's adaptive phase can stop early); ``None`` until the pools and the schedule are known.
planned.title: Planned

StepProgress.title: StepProgress

StepState.description: One planned step of a run: its status, time, error and, for a judging step, its progress.

progress.description: Judge windows done and planned (judging steps).

status.description: pending (planned, not started), running, completed, failed or cancelled.

StepState.title: StepState

StepStatus.description: The state of one step (also what ``run status`` reports for it).
StepStatus.title: StepStatus

description: What ``run start`` or ``run resume`` did: ran the run, handed it to a runner, planned it or estimated it.

rendered.description: For a plan handed to a runner: what it would submit, per job (script or YAML).
rendered.title: Rendered

run_dir.description: The run directory; null for a plan or an estimate of a new run.
run_dir.title: Run Dir

run_id.description: The run's id; null for a plan or an estimate of a new run.
run_id.title: Run Id

title: RunStartResult
